STRONACH, F. L.—Land purchase P.W.D., W. Aust., 1896; under sec. for wks., May, 1905.

STUART, ALEXR.—B. 1861; ed. St. And Univ.; regist. of impts. and expts., Sept., 1890; temporarily attached to H.M. toma, and trade marks branch of the patent London, 1897-8; comm. correspondent for and F.M.S. to intell. branch of B. of T., 1901.

STUART, HON. CHARLES ALLAN, B.A. (1)—B. 1864; ed. High schl., Strathroy, Ont., and Toronto Univ.; called to the bar, Ont., 1896; called to the bar, N.W.T., 1898; elec. first prov. legis., Alberta, 1905; judge of sup. ct., N.W.T., 1906; judge of supreme ct., Alberta, 1907; chancellor of univ. of Alberta, 1908.

STUART, JAMES.—Ed. St. John's C. Hurstpierpoint; matri. Lond. and Cape medal, Natal, Eng. lit. exam., 1891; clk. G.F. Pietermaritzburg, Feb., 1888; clk. and intell.
M., Eshowe, May, 1888; 1st clk. and interp. to s. comsnr. and ch. mag., Zululand, Feb., 1889; acted on various occasions as sec., res. comsnr. and ch. mag. sct., Zululand; interp. to Br. comsnr., Swaziland, 1894 to 1895; and in charge of Swazi reputations to Capetown and England in 1894; elected as Br. consul, Swaziland, 1895; R.M., Inga numa dist., Zululand, 1895; mag., Lower Tugela div., 1899; ast. mag., Durban div., 1901; mag. of colony, 1902; ast. sec. for native affairs, and sec. to the coun. for native affairs, 1st July, 1909.

STUBBS, REGINALD EDWARD.—B. 1876; ed. at Radley and Corpus Christi Coll., Oxford (exhibitioner); 1st cl. classical mods., 1897; 1st lit. hum., 1899; B.A., 1899; apptd., after compet. exam., 2nd cl. clk., C.O., Jan., 1900; ag. ast. cls. clk., May, 1907; 1st cls. clk., Dec., 1910; visited S. Sttlnts., F.M.S. and Hong Kong to inquire into question of revision of civ. ser. salaries, 1910-11; edited "Lucas' Historical Geography of the British Colonies," vol. i., 2nd edition, 1906.

SUETER, EDWARD BEAUMONT FRANK.—B. 1880; ed. Merton Coll., Oxford; cadet, Seylon civ. ser., Nov., 1903; off. ast. to gov't. gt., Colombo, Apr., 1905; ast. govt. agt., Kegalla, Nov., 1907; dist. judge, Kegalla, Feb., 1908; pol. mag., Kandy, Jan., 1910.

SULLIVAN, WILLIAM WILFRED, K.C.—Born P.E.I., 1843; called to the bar 1867; elected to legislature in 1872, and has continuously represented the same constituency; created a Q.C. by the gov't. of P.E.I., 1876, and by the gov't. gen. of Canada 1879; is a dep. judge in the admity. ct., was a mem. of the exec. coun., holding the office of regis.-gen., Apr., 1873, till Sept., 1876; leader of the Opposition in the legislature in 1877; prime min. and atty. and advoc.-gen. in 1879, has been a deleg. representing the prov. gov't. on several occasions in Canada, and was a deleg. to England in 1886, to confer with the impl. gov't. regarding the terms of confederation between P.E.I. and Canada; ch. just., P.E.I., 1889.

SURMON, WILLIAM BOWKER.—Sub.-inspr., Bechuana land Prot. pol., 1897; ast. res. mag. in Western Kalahari, 1907-1908; inspr. Bech. Prot. police, 1909.

SUTER, WM. CHAS.—Ast. master, govt. English schls., Singapore, 22nd Nov., 1884; ch. clk., col. sec.'s office, 1st July, 1888; shorthand reporter to leg. coun. in addition to other duties, 1st July, 1897.

SUTHERLAND, A. R.—M.A., Aberdeen Univ.; Science mast., Glen Urquhart H.G. schl., 1903-5; ast. mast., Campbelltown gram. schl., 1905-6; ast. mast., Queen's Coll., Hong Kong, 1906; lecturer in biology, Hong Kong Coll. of med., 1909-1910; ag. ast. master, pol. schl., 1909.

SUTHERLAND, GEORGE.—B. 1877; ast. man., Barbuda, Leeward Is., 1st Oct., 1908; ag. man. from 15th June, 1910.

SUTHERLAND, REAY MACKAY.—Sub.-inspr., Bechuana land Prot. pol., 1906.

SUTHERLAND, HON. ROBERT FRANKLIN, K.C., B.A.—B. 1859; ed. pub. and high schls., Newmarket and Windsor, Ontario, and Toronto and Western Unive.; called to the Bar, 1886; K.C., 1898; elec. to H. of C., Canada, 1900; re-elected 1904 and 1908; speaker of H. of C., 1905-1908; judge, High Court of Just., Ontario, 1909.

SUTHERLAND, WM.—Apptd. to Fiji civ. ser., Jan., 1880; clk. recr.-gen.'s office, Sept., 1880; clk., registr.-gen., Jan., 1882; stip. mag. of the col., Apr., 1883; ag. collr. of cust., Sept., 1897; ag. recr.-gen., Mar., 1898; native comsnr., 1898; ag. col. sec. and recr.-gen., Jan., 1903.

SUTTOR, THE HON. SIR FRANCIS B., KT. BACH. (1903).—B. 1839; postmr.-gen., N.S. Wales, Aug., 1880, to Nov., 1881; min. of pub. instruction, 1881 to 1883, and again, 1891-4; representative of col. at col. confce., Ottawa, 1894; pres. of legis. coun. of N.S. Wales, June, 1903.

SWAIN, ALFRED WILLIAM.—Clerical ast., regis.'s off., Barbados, 1879; jun. clk., G.P.O., Br. Guiana, June, 1881; 3rd cls. clk., Jan., 1883; 2nd cls., Dec., 1889; 1st cls., Apr., 1900; ch. clk., Sept., 1900; ag. postmr.-gen., May, 1901, to May, 1902; and Aug. to Dec., 1904; postmr.-gen., 18th May, 1907; 2nd lieut. Br. Guiana volunteers, 1889, ditto militia, 1891; lieut., 1892; capt., 1895; maj., 1900; ag. comdt. of local forces, July, 1901, to Feb., 1902; Hythe certif., 1893; Colonial and Aux. forces long service medal; recd. thanks of govt. on retiring in 1902, and retains rank of Major.

SWAIN, ARTHUR CLAUDE.—2nd clk., crown lands dept., Br. Guiana, Oct., 1879; ast. comsry., May, 1882; dist. ditto, July, 1881; is a J.P.

SWAIN, GEORGE LLEWELLYN DOUGLAS.—B. 1858; 1st clk. and bookkeeper, pol. dept., British Guiana, Apr., 1882; inspr. of pol., May, 1884; ch. inspr., Mar., 1892; ag. dep. inspr.-gen., July to Sept., 1893; on special service with Mr. McTurk, Feb., 1895, to take over Uruan from Venezuelans, remaining in command there till July, 1895; volr. in Ashanti expdn., Nov., 1896, to Mar., 1896; mentioned in despatches (star); two months' training with R.I.C. at Dublin, 1890; Hythe, P.S., and 1st cl. ambulance certifs.; ag. dep. inspr.-gen., Aug., 1898, to Jan., 1899; promoted ch. county inspr., and 2nd in command, 18th Nov., 1899; ag. inspr.-gen., 10th May to 21st Aug., 1900; servd. on comsn. apptd. to inquire into admstrm. of poor law relief, 1900; ag. inspr.-gen. of police, and col. comdt. of militia, 8th May to 3rd Sept., 1902; deputy inspr.-gen. of police, Trinidad, 30th September, 1903; ag. inspr.-gen. of constab. and comdt. of local forces with local rank of lieut.-col. and seat in exec. and legis. couns., 7th May to 10th Nov., 1903; ditto, with seat in legis. coun., 15th Apr. to 16th Sept., 1907; inspr.-gen. of constab. and comdt. local forces, 17th Sept., 1907.

SWAN, ROBERT ABRAHAM.—B. 1849; matric. at Madras Univ., Dec., 1868; passed special law test prescribed for uncoventional supts. and asst.-supts. of pol.; 2nd class inspr. of pol. in the Cuddapah dist., Madras, May, 1870; in Aug., 1871, 1st class; May, 1874, passed in Telugu; Oct., 1876, special ast. to sub-collr. and joint mag. of Cuddapah for famine relief duty, and in same month apptd. mag. with 1st class powers, and placed in charge of the Kadri and Madnapully Taluqs of Cuddapah dist.; in Feb., 1877, stip. mag. Mauritius; Jan., 1878, stip. mag. of Flaqc; and in Aug., 1879, Grand Port and Savanne; mem. of comsn. to frame reguls. under "labour ordinance of 1878"; member of Lincoln's Inn, 1882; called to the bar, 1887; stip. mag. Br. Guiana, Nov., 1883; in July, 1884, sent on special duty to Madras to organise an emigrn. agency for Br. Guiana; sheriff, Essequibo co., Dec., 1887; chmn. lands titles inquiry comsn., Feb., 1890; a revising barrister under Br. Guiana Constitn. Order, 1891; sheriff of Berbice and mag. New Amsterdam, 1892; acted as pol.
imag., Georgetown, Feb., 1890, and Oct., 1894, to Apr., 1895; mem. of comm. on poor-relief, 6th Apr., 1900; chairman of ditto, 7th Sept., 1900; appt. as pol. mag., Georgetown, confirmed by S. of S., 1st Oct., 1900; ag. puisne judge, sup. ct., 1st Oct., 1900; puisne judge, Trinidad, 3rd Aug., 1903; ag. ch. just., Trinidad and Tobago, 7th July to 12th Oct., 1904, and 26th June to 30th Oct., 1906; 1st puisne judge, Oct., 1906.

SWAYNE, CHARLES RICHARD, C.M.G.(1906).—Stip. mag., Fiji; inspr. of native taxes, 1876; stip. mag. and commr. of sup. ct., Lau prov., 1878; sent to Kadavu with special authority in native matters, 1879 and 1880; inspr. of Indian and Polynesian labourers, Lau prov., 1883; stip. mag., reg'ar, and commr. of sup. ct. at Levuka, 1885; returned to Lau, 1886; asst. native commr., Lau, 1888; ag. Br. res., Gilbert and Ellice Is., and special judicial commr. for trial of certain cases, Oct., 1893, to Nov., 1895; stip. mag., Rewa, and commr., Naitasiri, 1898; ag. native commr., and mem. exec. coun., 29th July, 1901, to 11th Sept., 1902; commr., Naitasiri, Sept., 1902; ag. commr., Rewa, 27th May to 31st Dec., 1903; offl. mem. legis. coun., 7th Apr., 1905; ret. 1906.

SWAYNE, COLONEL ERIC JOHN EAGLES, K.C.M.G. (1910).—C.B.—Joined Indian staff corps; entd. army, 1883; served in Burmah, 1886-87 (medal with clasp); spec. duty, Somaliland reconnaissance, 1890-92; served Uganda Mutiny and Jubaland, 1898 (medal with clasp); commanded Somaliland field force, 1901-2 and 1902-3 (brevet, medal and clasp); O.C. troops, Somaliland, 1904, with local rank brig.-gen.; intell. branch, headqrs., India, 1902-3 (McGregor medallist); commr., comdr.-in-chief and consul-gen., Somaliland Prot., 1st Mar., 1902; commr. and comdr.-in-chief, ditto, 23rd June, 1904; gov., B. Honduras, 21st Mar., 1906.

SWEENEY, GEORGE WILLIAM, B.A., LL.B. (Cape).—Asst. mast. Boys' Model Primary Schi., Pietermaritzburg, Natal, Feb., 1887; house mast., Maritzburg Coll., 1st Aug., 1888; resig. 30th Sept., 1895; clerical asst., col. office, 30th Oct., 1896; 3rd cl. clk., crown sol'r's office, 1st Feb., 1897; 2nd cls. clk., atty.-gen.'s office, 1st July, 1898; accnting. offr., atty.-gen.'s dept., 1st July, 1898; apptd. ch. clk. of the legis. assem., 1st Feb., 1901; sec. to party reprsntn. comm., Dec., 1903; law lecturer to Natal law soc., June, 1904; has acted as sec., law dept., and as asst. under sec.

SWEENEY, J. W.—Asst. traffic man., Uganda rly., Aug., 1898.

SWEET-ESCOTT, SIR E. B., K.C.M.G. (1904), C.M.G. (1895).—B. 1857; ed. Somersetshire Coll., Bath, and at Balliol Coll., Oxon.; exhibitioner, Worcestershire Coll., Oxon., June, 1876; 2nd class classical mods., June, 1878; 3rd class in mod. hist. finals, June, 1880; B.A., July, 1880; classical prof. at the Roy. Coll., Mauritius, June, 1881; prec. writer, col. sec.'s office, Feb., and 2nd asst. col. sec., Apr., 1886; ag. col. sec., 1889; ag. col. sec., Br. Honduras, Mar., 1893; admst. the govt. of that col., Apr. to Nov., 1893; col. sec., Br. Honduras, 1894; admst. govt., Apr. to Nov., 1895, again in 1897; ag. 1st class clk., C.O., Jan., 1898; admstr. of the Seychelles Is., Aug., 1899; assumed govt., 20th Nov., 1899; gov. and comdr.-in-chief, Oct., 1903; gov., B. Honduras, 15th Apr., 1904; gov., Leeward Is., 30th Jan., 1906.

SWETTENHAM, SIR F. A. THELSTANE, G.C.M.G. (1909), K.C.M.G. (1897), C.M.G. (1886).—B. 1850; cadet, S. Stiltsm., July, 1870; passed final exam. in Malay, July, 1872; asst. collr. of land rev. for P. and Prov. Wellesley, Aug., 1872; collr. of rev., July, 1873; J.P. and mag. and commr. of requests, Penang, May, 1874; sent on commissions to Perak in Jan., June, and July, 1874; asst. res., Selangor, Dec., 1874; gazetted temporarily as res. of Selangor, 22nd Oct., 1875; took charge of the residency in Perak, the murder of the res., Nov., 1875; dep. comm. Perak, Nov., 1875; mentioned in despatches; asst. col. sec. for native states, Mar., 1876; col. sec., July, 1881; Br. res., Selangor, 1882; commr. for S. S. and Malay States Exhibition, 1883-84; ag. Br. res., Perak, 1884, to Jan., 1886; exec. commr. for S. S. Malay States, Col. and Ind. Exhibition, 1886; res., Perak, 1889; res.-gen., Malacca States, 1896; admst. govt. S. S., Feb., 1901; gov., Perak, 1904; mem. of royal comm. on Mauritius, 1909.

SWETTENHAM, SIR J. A., K.C.M.G. (1892), C.M.G. (1892).—B. 1846; ed. Clare Coll.; scholarship, May, 1867; writer, Ceylon service; ag. pol. mag., Harrisspatu, Feb., 1870; pol. Kayts, Sept., 1870, continuing to act at Harrisspatu; ag. asst. govt. agt., Galle, Dec., 1871; landing and tide survr., Galle, June, 1872; collr. of customs, Jaffna, Oct., 1872, to coll. to act at Galle; ag. dist. judge, Matara, 1873; 2nd asst. col. sec., and clk. of the coun., 1876; rec.-gen., Cyprus, 1883; audt., Ceylon, 1891; col. sec., S. S., 1895; admst. June to Aug., 1895, from Mar. to Dec., 1896; from Dec., 1899, to Feb., 1901; gov., Br. Gen., 1901; govr., Jamaica, 14th July, 1904; ret. 1907.

SWINBURNE, HON. GEORGE, C.E.—B. M.I.A. for Hawthorn, Victoria, since 1892; mem. of pub. acct. comm., 1902-3; mem. Hawthorn comm., 1898-1904; mayor, 1904; min. of water supply, Victoria, since Apr., 1904; also min. of agric. since Nov., 1904.

SWINDELL, REV. FRANK GUTHRIE, D.D. (Oxon.).—Chap., Selangor, May, 1902; chap., Malacca, June, 1906; ag. col. chap., Singapore, Apr., 1907, to Jan., 1908.

SYDNEY, LORD ARCHBISHOP OF MONTREAL, JOHN CHARLES WRIGHT, B.A., M.A., D.D. Formerly curate of Kilworth-Beauchamp, 1888; Bradford, 1888-1893; lect., 1893-1895; vicar of Ulverston, 1893-1895; St. George's, Leeds, 1895-1904; can. res. of Manchester Cathedral, 1904-1909; rector of St. George's, Hulme, Manchester, 1904-1909; chaplain to the Duke of Manchester, 1904-1909; archdeacon of Manchester, 1909; consecrated Lord Archbishop Sydney, 24th Aug., 1909; Primate of Australia, 1910; author of "Thoughts on Modern Church Life and Work."

SYER, WM. CHAVALLIER.—B. 1873; ed. Eastbourne; qualified at asch. of musk., Hertford, Feb., 1901; asst. dist. commr., S. Nigeria, Jan., 1901; ag. dist. commr., Degema, Jan., 1902; asst. transport offr., Aro field force, No. column, 1901-1902 (medal with clasp); ag. dist. commr., Degema, July, 1903, to Jan., 1904; polit. offr., Ekpaflia field force, No. 2 column, Oct.-Dec., 1904; promoted dist. commr., Ist April, 1905; dist. commr., Akpiko, Aug. to Oct., 1905; polit. offr., Abakaliki, Oct., 1905, to Jan., 1906; dist. commr., Degema, Jan. to May, 1906; dist. commr., Abeokuta, May to Sept., 1906; dist. commr., Sapele, Feb. to June, 1907; ag. prov. sec. and ag. asst. prov. commr., Cent. Prov.
TARRANT, HUMPHREY MILNER.—Civ. servant, dept. of civ. instr., N.S. Wales, 1892-96; clk., Uganda Prot., 1897; in charge of transport at Wakoli, Busoga, 1898; in charge of Luba's station, 1899-1900; ag. collr., Busoga and Bukedi, 1900; ag. collr., Toro, 1901; asst. treas., 1902; 2nd asst. treas., 1904; 1st asst. treas., 1909; ag. dep. treas., Uganda Prot., from June, 1909, to Jan., 1910; and from May to Dec., 1910; mutiny medal with 2 clasps (Uganda, 1897-98).

TASCHEREAU, RIGHT HON. SIR H. E., KT. BACH. (1902), K.C., LL.D., P.C. (1904).—B. 1836 puisne judge, sup. ct., Quebec, 1871; puisne judge, supreme ct. of Canada, 1878; ch. just. of Canada, 1902-6; mem. of privy coun., 1904.

TASMANIA, BISHOP OF, RIGHT REV. JOHN EDWARD MERCER, D.D., OXON.—B. 1856; rector of St. Michael, Manchester, 1889-1896; of Gorton, Manchester, 1897-1902; bishop of Tasmania since 1902.

TATE, FRANK, I.S.O. (1903).—B. 1863; director of education, Victoria, Apr., 1902.

TATE, HARRY RUSSELL.—Ed. at Sherborne schl.; asst. collr., E. Africa Prot., 16th Dec., 1897; offr. in charge, E. Africa Transport, Ashanti Field Force, Aug., 1900; transport offr., Ogaden Punitive Force, Jan., 1901; collr., 8th May, 1901; Ashanti medal, 1900; Jubaland medal, 1901.

TAUBMAN-GOLDIE, P.C. (1898). THE RT. HON. SIR GEORGE DASHWOOD, K.C.M.G. (1887).—B. 1846; founder and dep. chmn. of the Royal Niger Co.; chmn., 1895.

TAVERNER, HON. SIR JOHN WILLIAM, KT. BACH. (1909).—B. 1854; mem. of Swan Hill Shire coun., Victoria, 1879; twice pres. and resig. in 1889; M.L.A. for Donald and Swan Hill, 1898 to 1904; mem. of first rlyw. standing comttee., min. of agric., comntr., of pub. wks., and vice-pres. of bd. of lands and wks., 1894-1899, min. of lands and agric., and pres. of bd. of lands and wks., 1902 to 1904; agent-gen. for Victoria in London, Feb., 1904; re-apptd. ditto, Feb., 1907.

TAYLOR, ARTHUR WM. FORBES.—B. 1857; 4th clk., treas., Natal, June, 1878; 3rd clk., Apr., 1879; 2nd elk., July, 1881; 1st elk., audit office, Mar., 1884; inspr., audit dept., 1897; ch. inspr., 1903.

TAYLOR, BASIL REGINALD HAMILTON, F.R.A.S.—B. 1865; entd. R.N. 1878; served in Egyptian war, 1882 (medal and clasp, Khedive's bronze star); lieut., 1888; served on Mediterranean, N. America, and W. India, China, and home stations; res. comm., 1898; rejoined R.N. as comdr. (emergency list), 1906; asst. harbmr., Hong Kong, July, 1899; ag. harbmr., Mar., 1900, to June, 1901, Sept., 1903, to Feb., 1914, and Aug. to Nov., 1905; M.L.C., June, 1900, to June, 1901, Sept., 1903, to Feb., 1904, and Aug. to Nov., 1905; ag. A.S.P. in addition, Oct., 1904, to Nov., 1905; harbmr., marine mag., emigrn. and cust. offr., supt. of imports and exports, regist. of shipping, supt., mercantile marine off., agent of C.I.B., B. of T., and fiscal authority under Brussels Sugar Convention, Mar., 1907; M.L.C., Sept., 1907, to Sept., 1908.

TAYLOR, EDWIN.—B. 1881; apptd., after compet. exam., elk. of the 2nd div. of the civ. ser., and assigned to C.O., Jan., 1901; served with I.Y. in S. African war, 1901-02 (medal and four clasps); re-apptd. to 2nd div., and assigned to B. of T., 1902; clk., P.W.D., B.C. Africa
Prot., July, 1906; treasy. ast., Uganda, Jan., 1909.

TAYLOR, FRANCIS BRYANT OLUDELE.—Ed. at C.M.S. Collegiate schl., Lagos; 3rd cls. certif., Lond. Coll. of Preceptors, 1903; 2nd cls. clk., audit dept., Lagos, Feb., 1907.

TAYLOR, FRANK.—Architectural ast., P.W.D., Cape Town, 3rd Nov., 1909, to 8th Jan., 1901; on active serv., lieut. in irregular corps, 8th Jan., 1901, to 7th Apr., 1902; chief draughtsman, P.W.D., O.R.C., 18th Apr., 1902; ch. architect, 1st July, 1905.

TAYLOR, JOHN.—B. 1863; entd. Royal Navy, 1883; served in Soudan war, 1884-5 (medal and Khedive's bronze star); impl. prison serv., Lond., Dec., 1887, to June, 1897; ch. warder, Belize pris., B. Hond., July, 1897; keeper of prisons, 1898; ag. dist. comsnr., Toledo, 1st Apr. to 5th Sept., 1905; ditto, Stann Creek, 12th Jan. to 29th May, 1906; ditto, El Cayo, 6th July, 1906, to 15th Apr., 1907; ditto, Stann Creek, 19th June to 17th July, 1907; ditto, Orange Walk, 18th July to 4th Sept., 1907; ditto, Stann Creek, from 6th Sept. to 30th Dec., 1907; ditto, Orange Walk, 7th Jan. to 13th Oct., 1908; ditto, Belize, offl. recr. in bank., and offl. adminstr., 23rd Oct., 1908, to 22nd May, 1909; J.P. for the colony, 1908; ag. dist. comsnr., Stann Creek, 12th July to 31st Aug., 1909; ditto, Toledo, 3rd to 13th Sept., 1909; ditto, El Cayo, 1st Oct., 1909.

TAYLOR, SIR W. T., K.C.M.G. (1905), C.M.G. (1895).—B. 1848; collr. of customs and excise, Larnaca, 1879; ch. collr. of customs, Cyprus, 1882; ag. recvr.-gen., Nov., 1883, to Feb., 1884; ag. comsnr., Larnaca, in addition to his own duties, 1883 and 1885; ag. recvr.-gen. in addition to duties as ch. collr. of cust., Jan. to Nov., 1887; recvr.-gen. and ch. collr. of cust. and excise, 1891; audr.-gen., Ceylon, May, 1895; ag. col. sec., Ceylon, Oct., 1895, to Feb., 1896, Mar. to Dec., 1896, Mar. to Nov., 1899, and Apr., 1900, to Nov., 1901; col. sec., S. Settns., June, 1901; admntd. govt. of S. S., Oct., 1903, to Apr., 1904, and Feb. to June, 1906; ag. recvr.-gen., F.M.S., Sept., 1904; confirmed, Jan., 1905; agent in London for F.M.S., Oct., 1910.

TEETZEL, HON. JAMES, LL.D.—B. 1853; ed. Woodstock and Galt (Ontario) collegiate insts.; called to the bar, 1877; K.C., 1890; elec. bencher, law soc., Upper Canada, 1891, 1896 and 1900; mayor of Hamilton, Ontario, 1890-1900; unsuccessful candidate for H. of C., 1900; justice, high ct., Ontario, 1903; LL.D., MacMaster Univ., 1907; chrmn., Ontario parole bd., 1910; comsnr. for revision of Ontario statutes, 1908-09-10.

TEMPANY, HAROLD AUGUSTINE, B.Sc.(Lond.), F.I.C., F.C.S.—B. 1881; ast. agric. chemist, Leeward Is., 1903; ag. govt. chemist and ast. of agric., July to Dec., 1906, and Jan. to Nov., 1908; govt. chemist and ast. of agric., Leeward Is., Nov., 1909.

TEMPLEMAN, HON. WILLIAM.—B. 1844; apptd. a senator of Canada, 1897; sworn of the priv. coun. and min. without portfolio, 1902; min. of inland rev. and mem. for Victoria, B.C., 1906; min. of inland rev. and of mines, 1907; mem. for Comox-Athi, B.C., 1909.

TEMPLER, FREDERIC GORDON.—Ed. at Harrow and at Trin. Coll., Camb.; called to the bar, Inn. Tem., Nov., 1872; went the W. circuit; apptd. dist. judge, Kyrenia, Cyprus, 1882; ag. puisne judge, sup. ct., May to Oct., 1888; Nov., 1888, to Feb., 1889; Jan. to Mar., 1890; and May to Sept., 1891; dist. judge, Larnaca, 1891; Queen's advoc., Cyprus, 1893; county ct. judge, 1898.

TENNANT, HERCULES, C.M.G. (1876); Barrister-at-law, Inn. Tem.; advoc., sup. Cape Col., 1873; sec. of law comsnr., represented Caledon in house of assm., lieutenant, D.E.O.V.R., 1878-81; extra A. to gov. and comdr-in-chief, July, 1879; w. in Basuto war, 1880-81 (medal), with capt., as ast. staff offr. to Gen. Clarke, and afterwards to Col. Carrington, C.M.G., to ch. just., 1882; librarian of the sup. ct.; ast. regis., sup. ct., and official rev.-authorised edition of Cape statutes, 1884; regis., ct. of appeal, Mar., 1886; J.P. for town and dist., and Capt. dist., July, 1886; taxing offr., sup. ct., Sept., 1884, and A. Dec., 1885; Apr. and Oct., 1886; Mar. and 1887; and Oct., 1887, to Jan., 1889; taxing Feb., 1889; high sheriff, Oct., 1889; regis., sup. ct., 1894; sec. to law dept., Transvaal, June, 1901; J.P., 1901; advocate of sup. 1902; examiner of candidates for admissible conveyancers, 1902; M.L.C., 1906; editor compiler of "The Notary's Manual"; "Justice of the Peace's Manual"; "Rules of the Chronological Table and Index of the Law of the Colony, 1714-1883"; "Master Servants Laws of the Colony"; joint editor authority) of a revised edition of "The Statutes, 1652-1886, and of the Griqualand Statutes"; also compiled (under auth.) "The Index of Government Proclamations Notices, 1803-1881."

TENNYSON, Rt. Hon. Lord, 2nd B. (U.K.), creat. 1884), G.C.M.G. (1903), K.C. (1889), HALLAM TENNYSON, succeeded 1902; poet laureate, 1850-92.—B. 1852; ed. Marl. Trin. Coll., Camb., and Inner Temple; J. Hants; mem. of Marl. Coll. exec. compared his father's memoir, published in S. Australia, 1899; gov.-gen., Commonwealth Australia, 1902-1904.

TEW, GEORGE McLEOD.—Indian pol., 1893-7; Uganda rly. pol., 1899-1903; ast. supt. of pol., E. Africa Prot., 1st Apr., 1904.

THAINE, ROBERT NIRMANN.—B. 1877; Eastbourne Coll. and St. John's Coll., Camb.; B.A.; cadet, Ceylon civ. ser., Nov., 1898; ast. to govt. agt. S. Prov., Apr., 1899; Prov., Aug., 1900; comsnr. of requests and mag., Balapitiya, June, 1901; off. ast. to agt., Ratnapura, Dec., 1901; ast. govt., Kalutara, Mar., 1902; dist. judge, Badulla, 1902; pol. mag., Kandy, May, 1904; landings cust., Colombo, Sept., 1904; ast. govt., Trincomalee, June, 1906; Puttalam, Aug., dist. judge, Jaffna, July, 1908.

THATCHER, J.—Ed. at Bristol Gram., examr. of loan acts., audit dept., O.R.C., Jan., 1904; examr. of accts., dist. 1st July, 1904.

THOMAS, E. J.—Entered Victoria College, 1852; receiver of revenue, etc., 1863; sec. to numerous boards and comsnrs.; privy to Sir B. O'Loughlin, Bart., 1881; sec., privy dept., 1883.

THOMAS, HON. JOSIAH.—B. 1863; M.L. New South Wales, 1894-1901; elected to H. of R., C. of A., 1901; re-elected in 1903; 1906; P.M.G., C. of A., Apr., 1910.

THOMLINSON, ROBT.—Intermediate Ed. Lond. (economics and polit. science); scholar of Lond. Schl. of Economics and Pol. Science; 2nd div. clk., nat. educn. off., Irel.
THOMPSON, WILLIAM AUSTIN.—2nd cl. supervsr. G. Coast, Apr., 1894; ag. ast. treas., Cape Coast Castle, Mar., 1895; cashr., Accra, Mar., 1896; ag. ast. treas., Apr., 1896; 1st cl. supervsr., Sept., 1897; sent on serv. in hinterland, Feb., 1898; invalided and retd. from West Afr., Feb., 1900; treas., etc., Falklands, July, 1901; mem. exec. and legis. couns.; ag. col. sec., in addition to duties as treasr., May to Nov., 1902, Apr., 1903, to Jan., 1904, July to Sept., 1905; and from June to Nov., 1909; in charge of headqrs. during govr.'s visit to W. Falklands, Aug., 1909.

THOMPSTONE, SYDNEY WILSON, C.M.G. (1906).—B. 1863; F.R.C.P. (Edin.), F.R.C.S. (Edin.), D.P.H. (Camb.); form. house surg., Roy. Infir., Glasgow; apptd. dist. med. offr., Oil Riv. Proteo. (now S. Niger), Mar. 22nd, 1893; ast. prin. med. offr., 1897; ag. prin. med. offr., Aug.-Nov., 1898; Nov., 1899, to June, 1900, and June, 1901, to Oct., 1902; prin. med. offr., N. Nigeria, May, 1903.

THOMSON, ALEX. MCDONALD.—Ed. Abdn. Univ., M.A.; 1st class hon. math., 1883; ast. prof. of math., Aberdeen, 1886-7; Bacon scholar, Gray's Inn, 1888; cadet, Hong Kong, 1887; attached to C.O., 1888; passed cadet, Dec., 1890; ag. supt., Victoria gaol, Apr., 1891, to Mar., 1892; ag. clk. of couns. Jan., 1891, to Oct., 1892; ag. ast. col. sec., Mar. to Oct., 1892; ag. registr.-gen. and provisional mem. exec. and legis. couns., 1893; ag. ast. col. sec., 1884; ag. col. treas., Mar., 1895; and mem. exec. and legis. couns.; mem. governing body of Queen's Coll., 1894; postmr.-gen., 1897; col. treas., and mem. exec. and legis. couns., 1898; ag. col. sec., Apr., 1892, Nov., 1903, to July, 1904, and in 1907, 1909 and 1910; has served on various comtees. and commsn.

THOMSON, HON. DUGALD.—B. 1848; M.L.A., New South Wales, 1894, 1895, and 1898; mem. of Commonw. parl., Mar., 1901, Dec., 1903, and Dec., 1906; min. for home affairs, ditto, Oct., 1904.

THOMSON, JOHN HASTINGS.—B. 1873; ed. Wallace Hall Academy, Dumfries-shire, Scotland; apptd. ast. dist. offr., Somaliland, May, 1901; ag. consul, Berbera, Sept., 1901, to Aug., 1903; ag. dist. offr., Bulhar, Jan., 1904-5; polit. offr. with Gen. Swayne in Abyssinia, Mar. to Apr., 1905; polit. offr. with troops on Abyssinian border, May to July, 1905; ag. sub-comsnr., Zeyla, 2nd June, 1905; Somaliland medal with clasp, 1902-4; dist. offr., Makhir Coast, Aug., 1906; ag. sub-comsnr., Zeyla, 5th June, 1907.

THORBURN, J. JAMIESON, C.M.G. (1907).—Writer, Ceylon, Oct., 1886; ag. govt. agt., N. Cent. Prov., Mar. to Aug., 1889; ag. pol. mag., Galle, Dec., 1893; ag. off. ast. to govt. agt., in various dists. from Oct., 1889, to 1895; ag. 2nd ast. col. sec., Jan., 1896; 2nd ast. col. sec., Jan. and Dec., 1898, and June, 1899; ag. ast. postmr.-gen., Jan., 1899; 2nd ast. col. sec., June, 1899; ag. sec. central irrigation board, Jan., 1900; principal ast. col. sec. and joint sec., loan board, May, 1900; senior prov. comsnr. (in anticipation of proposed amalgamation of the admstrs. of Lagos and S. Nigeria), performed duties of sec. to admstr. of S. Nigeria, dep. high comsnr., S. Nigeria, Mar. to June, 1905; ag. gov., Lagos, and ag. high comsnr., S. Nigeria, July, 1905; ag. col. sec., Lagos, 12th Feb. to 30th Apr., 1906; lieut.-gov. and col. sec., S. Nigeria, 1st May, 1906; dep. gov., 24th Dec., 1906, to 4th Jan., 1907, 6th-14th Jan., 1907, and 27th Jan. to 17th Mar., 1907; ag. gov., 14th May to 27th Oct., 1907; govr., Gold Coast, 24th Oct., 1910.
THORNHILL, PONSONBY.—Supernumerary offr., cust., B. Guiana, Aug.-Sept., 1887; astt. record clk., P.W.D., Oct., 1887; astt. to clk. of wks. (1st cls. offr.), P.W.D., New Amsterdam, May, 1888; 5th cls. offr., P.W.D., Apr., 1892; ag. clk. of wks. (1st cls. offr.) Berbice and distcts., Feb. to Aug., 1893; 5th cls. clk., G.P.O., June, 1896; clk., P.O. savings bank, Jan., 1899; 4th cls. clk., G.P.O., Jan., 1900; 3rd cls. clk., treasy., Georgetown, Jan., 1901; ag. cashier, June, 1904, to July, 1905, and May to Nov., 1908.

THORNTON, GEORGE.—M.D. (Edin.); M.R.C.P.(Lond.); D.P.H.(Oxford); house physcn., Edin. Royal Infirmy., 1890; house surg., Metropolitan hosp., Lond.; house surg., children's hosp., Hull; astt. med. offr., Tooting Fever hosp., 1893-99; civil surg. to H.M. forces in S. Africa; med. supt., Pretoria hosp., 1900-1908; med. supt., gen. hosp., Colombo, Ceylon, Nov., 1908.

THORNTON, SWINFORD LESLIE, B.A.—B.1853; Lincoln Coll., Oxon.; called to the bar, Lincoln's Inn, Nov., 1877; admitted to the bar, S. Sttlmts., Nov., 1886; registr., sup. ct.; comanr., ct. of requests, and collr. of stamps, Malacca, June, 1887; ag. sen. mag., Singapore, July, 1888; reg. sup. ct., and mag., Malacca, July, 1892; atty.-gen., St. Vincent, 1894; ag. admstr., Nov., 1894, to Mar., 1895; ag. ch. just., Nov., 1895; res. mag., Jamaica, 1896; mem. comtee. to revise rules and form res. mag. etc., 1897; mem. parochial bds. comanr.; and chrmn. house and land tax comtee., 1899; ag. puisne judge, 1901; puisne judge, S. Sttlmts., 22nd Mar., 1904; sen. puisne judge, Aug., 1906.

THORPE, WM. EDWARD.—Offr., cls. III., Ceylon civ. ser.; ed. St. Edmund's schl., Canterbury; cadet, Ceylon, 1891; office astt., Anuradhapura, 1892; ditto, Jaffna, 1894; ditto, Ratnapura, 1896; ditto, Colombo, 1896, with additional duties as astt. supt. pol.; astt. govt. agt., Kalutara, 1898; ditto, Chilaw, 1899; dist. judge, Matare, 1900; pol. mag., Colombo, 1903; dep. collr. cust., Colombo, 1905; dist. judge, Matare, May, 1908; ditto, Galle, Dec., 1908.

THREIFALL, WM. HERBERT.—B. 1875; apptd., after open compet., exam., to controller's off., London postal service, Apr., 1896; supt. of registn., G.P.O., Singapore, Oct., 1905; ag. supt. of mails, G.P.O., Singapore, Nov., 1905; supt. of registn., ditto, Sept., 1906; supt. of mails, Penang, Sept., 1907.

THUNDER, MAURICE.—Cadet, S. Sttlmts., Dec., 1905; ag. dist. offr., Penang, Sept., 1906; ag. dist. offr., Prov. Wellesley, Nov., 1907; passed final exam.in Malay, Jan., 1908; ag. 4th mag., Singapore, Apr., 1908; ag. astt. to atty.-gen., Dec., 1908.

TIBBITS, CHARLES KENT.—B. 1877; employed col. sec.'s off.; treas. and aud. off., Antigua, Apr. to Dec., 1894; clk. sav. bank, Jan., 1895; 1st clk., post off., Jan., 1898; ag. postmtr. in 1899, 1900, 1901, 1903, 1904, 1906; and from June, 1906, to Mar., 1907; postmtr. of Antigua, and federal postmtr. of Leeward Is., 1st Apr., 1907; apptd. a library trustee and a J.P., Antigua, 1910.

TIRBITS, ELWOOD D'ARCY.—B. 1880; ag. 4th clk., col. sec.'s off., Antigua, Jan., 1899, to Nov., 1900 (almost continuously); jun. audit clk., 1st Dec., 1900; 4th clk., col. sec.'s off., 8th July, 1901; ag. 3rd clk., 29th Aug., 1901, to 1st June, 1902, and 5th June, 1902, to 5th Mar., 1903; ag. priv. sec. to gov., 17th Oct., 1903, to 5th May, 1904; ag. 3rd clk., 24th Mar. to 1st Aug., 1905; ag. clk. to adminstr. and clk. to exec. coun., Dominica, 2nd Aug., 1905, to 5th Apr., 1906; ag. 2nd clk., col. sec.'s off., Antigua, and clk. to exec. coun., Antigua, from 6th Apr., 1906; 3rd clk., col. sec.'s off., Antigua, 23rd Sept., 1906, to 23rd Jan., 1907; ag. 2nd clk., ditto, and clk. to exec. sec. and supt. of govt. printing off., from 5th Sep., 1907, to 8th Mar., 1908; ag. astt. col. sec., 13th Nov. to 11th Dec., 1907, and from 11th 22nd Jan., 1908; ag. 2nd clk., 20th Apr., 19th Oct., 1908; and from 19th April, 1909.

TIBBITS, RICHARD WHITE LONGMUIR.—1846; ed. at high schl., Quebec and Lennoxville coll., formerly coroner, J.P., and sec. treas. Victoria, New Brunswick; elec. to legislative N.B., 1882; dep. prov. sec., N.B., 1885; clk. printer, 1895.

TICE, W. G.—B. 1867; apptd., after exam. 3rd cls. mess., C.O., 19th Feb., 1900; 2nd cls. 1st Feb., 1902.

TINNEY, LOUIS HERBERT JOHN, R.N.R.—B. 1873; apptd. dep. harbmr., Georgetown, B. Guiana, Apr., 1904; ag. harbmr., June, 1904; June, 1906, and May to Nov., 1907; has rec. R.H.S. silver medal for saving life at sea.

TOBIAS, M. S.—Clk., stats. branch, exec. off., Cape Town, Dec., 1901; 2nd clk., res. mkt., O.R.C., May, 1902; examr. of acts., dept., O.R.C., Aug., 1906.

TODD, JOHN SPENCER BRIDGES, C.M.G.—B. 1840; jun. clk., col. sec.'s office, Cape, 1860; 2nd clk. to C.C. and R.M., Swellendam, Dec., 1862; 2nd cls. clk. to C.C., Robertson, Nov., 1864; 1st clk. to C.C., Swellendam, May, 1867, to Aug., 1874, but was agt. and R.M., Swellendam, June, 1870, to Jan., 1872, and again during Sept. and Oct., 1872; corpdr. clk. to rly. engr. of the col. line, 1874, to Mar., 1875; clk. in charge of money and stamps, G.P.O., Capetown, Apr., 1875; employed on special service as sec. to govt. comanr. investigating the accs. balances of the col. treasy-chest, Capetown, May to Dec., 1875; was exec. comanr. of the col. at the Paris Exhibition of 1878; sec. col. sec.'s dept., Jan., 1876; in June, 1876, served with Sir H. White and Mr. Lawson (W. and Sir W. B. Gurdon (Treasury), on a comanr. to investigate the expenditure incurred by the Impl. and col. govts. in the Transkei in 1878; proceeded in June, 1881, on special ser. to Kimberley, with a view to adjusting the accounts of the prov. of Griqualand W.; acted as C.C. and reg. of deeds at Kimberley from Sept., Dec., 1881; and as astt. comanr. of Crown and pub. wks. in Capetown from Jan. to Apr., 1882; sec. and acct. to the agt. gen. for col. in London, Oct., 1882; agt. agt., 1895-6; ret., 1905.

TOLMIE, RODERICK FINLAYSON.—B. 1859; coll. schl., Victoria, British Columbia; clk. bank of B. Columbia (Caribou agency) 1874; B.C. govt. serv., 1877; gen. sec. B.C. owners assoc., 1899; re-entd. govt. serv. as min. of mines, 1902.

TOMALIN, HERBERT FREDERIC.—B. 1859; M.I.C.E., F.R.I. Br. Architects, and F.G.S. Northampton Gram. schl.; astt. to C.E. at L. and N.W. rly. wks., 1880-6; dist. clk., P.W.D., Ceylon, 1886-90; reported on proposed lighthouse sites, southern coast of Ceylon; dist. engnr. Colombo harbr., foresight drainage wks., 1887-8 and 1890-2; 2nd finan. officer astt. P.W.D., Ceylon, 1890-6; designed constructed post and telegr. bldgs., Colombo, 1892-5; dist. engnr., Colombo, 1893-6; dist. engnr. scheme for water supply to the town of Jacaré, Nov., 1896, to Apr., 1897; engnr., N.W. Prov. E. Prov., Aug., 1899, and scheme for a
supply to the town of Trincomalee and to the naval and military cantonment; prov. engr., Cent. Prov., Mar., 1903; ditto, W. Prov., Mar., 1904; asst. D.P.W., Jan., 1905; prov. engr., Cent. Prov., Sept., 1905; ditto, S. Prov., 31st Mar., 1908.

TOMKINS, STANLEY C., C.M.G. (1900).—Apptd. by F.O. as asst. dist. offr., Uganda, Feb., 1896, and ch. offr., Uganda Rifles, 26th Apr., 1897; served during mutiny in Uganda, 1897-8 (ment. in desp., medal with two clasps); dist. offr. in charge of Kavirondo, Aug., 1897; ag. sub-commr. in charge of Uganda Kingdom, May, 1900; jud. offr., Uganda Prot., 21st Mar., 1900; ag. sub-commr., W. Prov., May, 1902; sees, judge, May, 1903; sub-commr., Sept., 1904; in charge of Uganda Kingdom, Dec., 1904; ag. dep. commr., 19th May, 1906, to 20th Feb., 1907; in charge of Uganda Kingdom, 4th Dec., 1907, to 28th Sept., 1908; ag. dep. commr., 29th Sept., 1908; ag. gov., 29th Sept. to 19th Oct., 1908; ag. chief sec. to gov., 1st Nov., 1908; ag. gov., Uganda, 1909.

TONNET, LOUIS ARTHUR.—Joined Mauritius police, 16th Feb., 1885; transfd. to Seychelles, 1893; sub-inspr., 1st Mar., 1902; ag. inspr. since 8th May, 1907; a visiting magistrate for outlying islands.

TOOKER, H. P.—Ed. at Queen's Coll., Cork, Irel.; grad. bach. of engrg. at Queen's Univ. (now Royal Univ. of Irel.), 1879; artic. to borough engrg., Salford, 1880; apptd. asst. engrg. to munl. coun., Birkenhead, 1883; apptd. exec. engrg., p.w. dept., H. Kong, 1890; ag. dir. p.w., May to Aug., 1894, and again in 1900; ag. asst. dir. p.w., 1900; apptd. assoc. mem. inst. civ. engrgs., Dec., 1892; mem. of soc. arts, Feb., 1901.

TOPPIN, CHARLES SAMUEL.—B. 1866; ed. at Diocesan schl., Waterford, Ireland; served as book keeper and acctnt. with W. Australian land & co. (Great Southern rly.), 1887 to 1897; on taking over of line entd. gov't. ser. as sub-acctnt., rly. dept., 1st Mar., 1897; asst. acctnt., 1st July, 1900; ag. ch. acctnt., 1st July, 1903; aud-gen. for State of W. Aust., Feb., 1904; also dep. aud-gen. for Commonwealth, Feb., 1904, to Jan., 1906.

TORONTO, BISHOP OF, RIGHT REV. J. F. SWEENEY, D.D.—B. 1857; ed. at McGill Coll., Montreal, and Trin. Coll., Toronto; ordained, 1880; rector of St. Luke's, Montreal, 1880-82; hon. Canon, Toronto, 1889-1905; archdeacon of Simcoe, 1905; rector of St. Philip's, Toronto, 1882-1909; archdeacon of York, Toronto, 1906; bishop of Toronto, 1909.

TOTHELL, FRANCIS JAMES.—Extra asst. to postmtr.-gen., Ceylon, 28th Oct., 1898; asst. inspr. of post offices, Jan., 1899; asst. sec., cent. irrigtn. bd., 15th Jan., 1900; sec., ditto, and office asst. to dir. of irrigtn., 15th May, 1900; asst. acctnt., gen. treas., Jan., 1907.

TOUGH, JOHN.—B. 1879; ed. St. Andrew's Coll., Dublin; served 11 years in 42nd Hghts.; 1st cl. cert. of educn., 1896; cert. of mil. eng., 1898; Hythe cert. of musk. (distinguished) 1904; mounted infantry cert., 1905; served in South African War, 1899-1902; Queen's medal and 3 clasps; King's medal and 2 clasps; severely wounded at Magersfontein; sub.-inspr. of pol. and drill instr., St. Kitts, 1907; J.P., St. Kitts, 1907; ag. inspr. of pol. and adjt. of local forces, 1908; chmn. of tel. bd., 1908; estab. helio. commun. between St. Kitts and Nevis, 1909; sub.-inspr. of pol. mil. instr., inspr. of roads and works, inspr. of weights and meas., Montserrat, 1909; J.P., Montserrat, 1909; mem. bd. of health, 1910; sub.-inspr. of pol. and mil. instr., Antigua, 1910; ex-officio J.P. for Leeward Is.

TOWNER, H. V.—Mem. San. Inst., Assoc. mem. C.E.A.; asst. supt. of wks., S. Stltns., Mar., 1901; supt. of wks. and surveys, Malacca, Oct., 1904; ag. supt. of wks. and surveys, Singapore, Apr. to Sept., 1902, and from Nov., 1904, to Mar., 1908.

TOWNSEND, ALFRED ERNEST.—Ed. at Brisbane gram. schl.; asst. survr., G. Coast survey, 1902-1905; survr., E. Africa Prot., 24th Aug., 1905.

TOWNSEND, W. H. M.—Ch. offr., Uganda rly. lake steamers, June, 1903; comdr., July, 1905.

TOWNSEND, WM. RICHARD.—B.A., Dublin Univ., 1894; called to the bar, Ireland, 1894; atty.-gen., Gambia, 1st May, 1902; inspr. of schls., col. regis. and mem. of exec. and legis. couns. during tenure of atty.-generalship; ch. mag. and M.L.C., Gambia, 6th Nov., 1906.

TOWNSHEND, SIR CHARLES JAMES, Kt.-Bach. (1911).—B. 1844; ed. Collegiate sch. and King's Coll., Windsor Nova Scotia; B.A., B.C.L., D.C.L.; called to bar, 1866; Q.C., 1881; elec. to legis. assem., 1878 and 1882; H. of C., 1884; just. of the sup. ct. of N.S., 1887; ch. just. of N.S., 1907.

TOWNSON, HARRY WALLS, M.R.C.V.S.—Ch. inspr. of stock, Falkland Is., May, 1910.

TOZER, HON. SIR H., K.C.M.G. (1897).—B. 1844; formerly col. sec., Queensland; agt. gen. for Queensland in London, 1898.

TRAILL, FRANCIS STUART FORBES.—Asst. collr., E. Africa Prot., 10th Oct., 1898; collr., 1st Apr., 1903.

TRATMAN, DAVID WM.—Ed. at Clifton Coll., sohrl. of Univ. Coll., Oxford, 1900; B.A., 1904; cadet., Hong Kong, 1904; passed cadet, 1907; ag. asst. land offr. in New Territories, and register of land ct., Mar., 1907; mem. of land ct., June, 1907; ag. pol. mag. in New Territories, July, 1907; ag. asst. dist. offr., May, 1909; 2nd asst. registr.-gen., Sept., 1909; ag. supt. of imports and exports, May, 1910.

TRAVERS, A. K.—3rd clk., col. sec.'s office, Hong Rong, Oct., 1874; priv. sec. to Admstr. Austin, Mar. to Apr., 1877, and to Gov. Hennessy, Apr. to July, 1877; ag. 2nd clk., col. sec.'s office, July to Nov., 1877; 2nd clk., Dec., 1881, to May, 1883; priv. sec. to Admstr. Marsh, Apr., 1882, to Apr., 1883; asst. P.M.G., May, 1883; J.P., Dec., 1883; ag. P.M.G. and collr. of stamp rev., June, 1888.

TRAVERS, BENJAMIN.—B. 1849; dist. mag., Br. Honduras, June, 1882; excise offr., judge of civil juris., also coroner, ag. priv. sec. to gov'r., and clk. to exec. and legis. couns., 1886; undertook a journey over unexplored territory to bring into the colony Indian refugees from Guatemala, 1884; conferred with dissatisfied Indian chief, Gen. Tamay, on question of border delimit. and established amicable relations, 1887; commr., Famagusta, Cyprus, 1892; acted as local commr. of pol. in conjunction with own duties, July, 1898, to Oct., 1899, and at various other times.

TREACHER, SIR W. H., K.C.M.G. (1904), C.M.G. (1890), M.A. (Oxford).—B. 1849; ag. pol. mag., Labuan, Nov., 1871, to June, 1872; ag. col. sec. and audr., Oct., 1873; col. sec., audr., and pol. mag., Apr., 1877; admtd. the gov't., Dec., 1876, to Feb., 1877; and Oct., 1877, to Apr., 1880; mem. of the legis. coun., Dec., 1874. During the periods he admstd. the gov't. he acted as consul-
gen. in Borneo, and visited Sulu and N. Borneo in connection with Spanish claims; apptd. (1881) the first gov. of Br. N. Borneo, to Dec., 1887; again acted as admstr. of Labuan and consul-gen. in Borneo, from Feb., 1884, to Nov., 1885; and was instrumental in saving Brunei from an attack of the Limbang rebels; sec. to Perak, June, 1888; ag. res., Sept., 1888; res., Selangor, July, 1892; res., Perak, July, 1896; res.-gen., Fed. Malay States, Sept., 1901; ret., 1905.

TREFLÉ, HON. J. L.—M.L.A., N.S. Wales, 1907; hon. min. and asst. min. of agricult., Oct., 1910.

TREGEAR, EDWARD.—B. 1846; emig. to N. Zealand in 1863; apptd. Goldfields survr., 1867; in command Waikato native contingent, 1875; sec. labour dept. and ch. inspr. of factories, 1891; J.P., 1893; decoration from French Republic, 1896; regsr. of industrial unions, 1900; is author of "The Maori-Polynesian Dictionary," "The Paumotian Dictionary," "Fairy Tales of the South Seas," "A Dictionary of Mangareva," "The Maori Race," etc., etc.

TRENHOLME, HON. NORMAN W.—B. 1837; ed. McGill univ., B.A. and Chapman medal, 1863; B.C.L. and gold medal, 1865; D.C.L., 1887; prof., faculty of law, McGill univ., 1868-1888; dean, 1888-1896; K.C. and bottomer of the bar, Montreal, 1888-1889; counsel for Quebec in arbitn. between Ontario and Quebec and the Dominion, 1897-1901; judge, super. ct., Montreal, 1901-1904, and of K.B. and appeal ct., since June, 1904.

TRESIDDER, CAPT. TOLMIE JOHN, R.E., C.M.G. (1887).—B. 1850; was engrnr. for Malta drainage wks.

TRICKETT, W. J., M.L.C.—Postmr.-gen., N.S. Wales, May, 1883; min. of instruction, May, 1884, to Nov., 1885; chmn. of comtees, and dep. pres. of legis. coun., June, 1900.

TRINIDAD, BISHOP OF, RIGHT REV. JOHN FRANCIS WELSH.—Ed. at Christ Church, Oxford, B.A. (1881), M.A. (1886); D.D., Oxford Univ., 1904; consec. Bishop of Trinidad, 28th Oct., 1904.

TROTTER, J. F.—Asst. survr., great trigonometrical survey of India, for seven years; ensign W.I. Regt., 1870; lieut., 1871; 2nd sub-imigrn. agt. of Br. Guiana, Feb., 1872; sen. sub-imigrn. agt., Nov., 1872; in charge of imigrn. dept., Feb. to Sept., 1873; and ag. imigrn. agt.-gen. on several occasions; prot. of imigrts., Mauritius, Apr., 1881; special imigrn. comsrr., to India, May, 1883, to Apr., 1884, and May to Dec., 1889.

TROWBRIDGE, EDMUND.—B. 1881; ed. pub. model and high schls., Toronto, Ontario; asst. clk., exec. coun., 1906; sec., Alberta coal comsrr., 1907; sec., Alberta pork comsrr., 1908; dep. prov. sec. and regsr. of companies, prov. of Alberta, 1910.

TROWELL, WM. JOHN.—B. 1864; M.I.N.A.; engrnr. and shipwright survr. and examnr. of engnrns., Liverpool, Feb., 1898; inspr. under bd. of agric., Dec., 1898; inspr. of marine surveys, S. Stlmta, 16th Jan., 1903; on special ser. in England in connection with expropriation of Tanjung Pagar Dock Co., Ltd., July to Nov., 1905.

TRUMP, JOHN, M.I.C.E.—B. 1858; entd. P.W.D., Ceylon, 1878; in charge of convicts on Colombo breakwater construction, 1880 to 1883; services lent to native states, S. Stlmta., 1883 to 1886; transfed. to P.W.D., Perak, 1886; dep. state engnr., Perak, Feb., 1887; state engnr., May, 1901; ag. dir. of P.W., F.M.S., Apr., 1904, to Jan., 1906.

TUBOKU-METZGER, ALBERT EMERIC, B.A.—Ed. in C.M.S. Gram. schl. and Fourah Bay Coll., Sierra Leone; gained Fourah Bay Coll. foundation scholarship, Jan., 1877; grad. in Arts, June, 1881; first cls. hons in theology, Durham Univ., Dec., 1881; jun. cls. tutor, Fourah Bay Coll., 1881; entd. S. Leone civ. serv. as extra clk., secretar. and treas., 1st Mar., 1885; govt.'s office, 1886; col.-treas., 1887; served as finan. clk. in Yonni expdn. under Sir Samuel Rowe, 1887; ch. clk., registr.-gen.'s dept., 1890; registr. births and deaths, Freetown dist., 1890; polk. clk. and clk. of ct. of requests, Freetown, Apr., 1895; ag. registr.-gen., 1904 to 1905, and 1st asst. dist. commr., 1st May, 1905; apptd. Crown prosecutor in the Sept. sessions of the sup. ct. v Sherbro, Oct., 1908; is a J.P. for the col.

TUCKER, LESLIE.—Ed. at Liverpool Collegiate Insttn. and Univ. Coll., Liverpool; prelim. az. inter. B.A.; 1st cls. scholarship; 1st cls. burs. years certif. exam.; parchment certif., 1887; head master, govt. boys' schl., St. Helena, 1906; head master, senior schl., St. Helena, 1906; hon. sec., govt. Lace schl., 1908.

TUDOR, DANIEL THOMAS, K.C.—B. 1866; called to the bar, Gray's Inn, Nov., 1890; eq. u. also practised on West. Circ.; atty.-gen. of Grenada and St. Vincent, July, 1903; also sec. col. sec., Grenada, on several occasions; ag. just., Grenada, May to Oct., 1904, Nov., 1905, June to Nov., 1909; K.C., Grenada and St. Vincent, May, 1908; admnstr. govt. of St. Vincent, June, 1907, to Jan., 1908, and govt. of Grenada, May to June, 1908.

TUDOR, HON. FRANK Gwynne.—B. 1866; M.P. for Yarra, Victoria; pres. of Melbourne trades hall coun., 1900-1901; elec. to tr. H. of R., C. of A., 1901; min. of trade and com. C. of A., Apr., 1910.

TUPPER, THE RIGHT HON. SIR C., BAR. (creat., 1888), P.C. (1907), G.C.M.G. (1886), K.C.M.G. (1879), C.B. (1867), M.D., L.R.C.S. Edin. (1843).—Born 2nd July, 1821; is an M. and D.C.L. of Acadia Coll., Nova Scotia; gov. of Dalhousie Coll., Halifax (apptd. by Ar. of Parlmt., 1862); pres. of the Canadian med. assoc. from its formation, 1867, until 1871; mem. of exec. coun., and prov. sec. N.S., 1871-1860; and from 1863 to June, 1867; prime min. of prov. from 1864 until he ret. from office with his govt. on the Union Act coming into force, 1st July, 1867; deleg. to England on public business from N.S. govt., 1858 and 1865; from the Dominion govt., Mar., 1868; leader of the deleg. from N.S. to the union confec. at Charlottetown, 1864; to that in Quebec in same year, and to final conf. confec. in London, to complete terms of union, 1866-7; held patent of rank and precedence from Her Majesty Queen Victoria as an exec. coun., N.S.; sworn of the P.C., June, 1870, and pres. of that body until 1st July, 1872, when apptd. min. of int. rev.; min. of customs, Feb., 1873; resig. office with Sir John Macdonald, 5th Nov., 1873; min. of pub. wks., Oct., 1878; min. of rly. and canals, 1879; represented Cumberland in parlmt. for 29 years in N.S. Assem. from 1855 until confederation in 1867, and in the Commons from that year until he resig. his seat in the cabinet and was apptd. high comsrr. for Canada in London, May 24th, 1884; acted as exec. comsrr. for Dominion at the Antwerp Exhibn., 1885, and the Col. and Ind. Exhibn., London, 1886; resumed office in Canadian ministry as finance min., 1887; one of H.M.'s plenipotentiaries at fisheries confec. at Washington, 1887; re-apptd. high comsrr., May, 1888; joint plenip., with the Marquis de Dutferin.
and Sir J. A. Crowe, for negotiating a commercial arrangement between Canada and France, 1892; S. of S. for Canada, Jan., 1896; premier, Mar. to June, 1896; leader of opposition in H. of C., 1896-1900.

TUPPER, Hon. Sir Chas. Hibbert, K.C.M.G. (1893).—B. 1855; son of Sir C. Tupper, mem. of N.S. bar; grad. Harvard law schl.; mem., house of commons, Canada, 1882-1900; min. of marine and fisheries, 1888-1895; deleg. to Washington in connection with Behring Sea difficulty, 1890; Br. agt. for the arbitration with the U.S. on the Behring Sea question, 1892-3; min. of just., 1895; resig. 1896; mem. of priv. coun. for Canada.

TURGEON, William Ferdinand Alphonse, K.C., B.A.—B. 1877; ed. at New York city and Laval univ., Montreal; barrister; atty.-gen. of Sask., 23rd Sept., 1907; elec. to Sask. legis., 1907; re-elec., 1908.

TURNER, The Rt. Hon. Sir George, P.C., K.C.M.G. (1897), LL.D.—B. 1851; premier and treas. of Victoria, 1894-9 and 1900-1; represented the col. in London at H.M.'s Diamond Jubilee 1897; pres. of conf. of premiers at Melbourne, 1899; joined 1st Commonwealth ministry as treasurer, Jan., 1901; treas. in 2nd (Deakin) ministry; treas. in 4th (Reid-Turner) coalition ministry, 1904; retired from politics, 1906.

TURNER, GEORGE.—M.R.C.S., L.R.C.P. (Lond.), M.B., D.P.H. (Cantab.); lecturer on Hygiene, Guy's hosp., 1882-1895; examinr. for D.P.H., roy. coll. of phys. and surge., Lond., 1890-1895; employed by L.G.B. to report upon diphtheria, 1884; and by L.C.C. to inquire into epidemics of enteric fever and the sanitation of River Lea, 1894-95; med. offr. of health, Cape, 1895-1900; mem. of Cape med. coun., 1898-1900; dir. of govt. rinderpest experimental statn., Kimberley, 1897-98; med. offr. of health, Transvaal, 1st Aug., 1900; M.L.C.; census comnr., Transvaal, 1904; del. for Transvaal and O.R.C., Internat. Leprosy. conf., Bergen, 1909.

TURNER, James Pocson.—B. 1871; clk., pub. library, St. Kitts, 1890; clk., regis.'s off., St. Kitts, 1897; comnr. to administer oaths, 1898; clk. to mag., dist. "C," St. Kitts, May to Oct., 1905; 1st clk., regis.'s off., Antigua, 3rd May, 1906; clk. to trustees, sup. ct. library, 1906; clk. to regis. of jt. stock companies, Nov., 1906.

TURNER, Lewis James Barnettson.—B. 1886; ed. Edinburgh Univ. (M.A.); cadet, Ceylon civ. ser., Oct., 1908; off. asst. to gov't. agt., N.W. Prov., Dec., 1909.

TURNER, WILLIAM.—Ed. at Abdn. and Edin. Unive.; M.A. (Abdn.), 1876; M.B. Edin., 1879; M.D. 1881; rec. phy., roy. hosp. for sick chldrn., Edin., 1879; non-res. phys., roy. infirmy., Edin., 1889; res. accoucheur, Glasgow maternity hosp., 1881; mem. roy. med. soc., Edin., fell. obstetrical soc., Edin.; asst. surg. civil hosp., Gibraltar, 1882; also surg. civ. prison, med. offr. lunatic asyl., and dist. med offr., 1882; pub. vaccinator, pd. surg., 1888; surg. to col. hosp., Oct., 1889.

TUTCHER, WM. James, F.L.S.—B. 1867; ed. at Merchant Venturers schl., Bristol; entered Royal Gardens, Kew, 1888; asst. supt., botan. and forestry dept., Hong Kong, 1891; actg. supt. in 1893, 1894, 1897, 1900 to 1901, 1902 to 1903, 1905, 1906, 1907, 1908 and 1909; supt., 1910; late hon. lecturer on botany, coll. of med. for Chinese; author of "Gardening for Hong Kong."

TWEEDIE, Hon. Lemuel J., K.C., LL.D.—B. 1849; ed. at Presbyterian Coll.; admitted to bar, New Brunswick, 1871; mem. of legis., 1874-1878, 1886-1907; has represented Northumberland ever since, except during 1878 to 1882; survr.-gen., 1890; prov. sec., 1896; premier, 1900; represented N.B. at the King's Coronation, 1902; holds Canadian Militia long service medal; lieut.-gov. of New Brunswick, 3rd Feb., 1907.

TYLER, James Ernest.—Gov't. printer, S. Stltms., 1st July, 1905.

TYRRELL, Francis Graeme.—B. 1876; ed. Pembroke coll., Oxford (B.A.); cadet, Ceylon civ. ser., Oct., 1900; ag. priv. sec. to H.E. the governor, Aug., 1901; priv. sec. to H.E. the offr. admstg. the gov't., Apr., 1902; off. asst. to gov't. agt., Cent. prov., Jan., 1903-Dec., 1904; ag. asst. gov't. agt., Nuwara Eliya, Oct., 1904; seconded supt. of pol., N.W. prov., Aug., 1905, cent. prov., Mar., 1907; dist. judge, Badulla, Dec., 1908; asst. gov't. agt., Matale, Feb., 1909.

TYSER, Sir C. R., Kt. Bach. (1909).—Ed. at Rugby and Trin. Coll., Camb., M.A. (1872); called to bar, In. Tem., 1873; asst. ag. judic. comnr. and leg. adv., Cyprus, 1880-1; atty.-gen., Leeawards, 1886-9; pres. dist. ct., Kyrena, Cyprus, 1886; puisne judge, Cyprus, Jan., 1902; ch. just., 1906; author of "Marine Insurance Losses," 1894; wrote translation of Omar Hilmi Effendi's Evkaf Law, 1899; and of the Mejléjé, 1901.

TYSSEN, Francis Dashwood.—Ed. at Melbourne Church of England Gram. schl. and Trin. Coll., Melbourne Univ.; lieut. 2nd Scottish Horse, S. African War; inspr. of pol., E. Africa Prot., May, 1905; asst. dist. supt. of pol., 1st July, 1906.

UDAL, John Symonds.—Called to the bar, In. Tem., Michaelmas term, 1875, W. circuit; J.P. for co. of Dorset; dep. county court judge, 1885-6-7; atty.-gen. of Fiji, Aug., 1889; Admity. adv., Sept., 1889; ag. ch. justice for short periods in 1891-2-8; ag. legal asst. C.O., Feb. to Dec., 1900; ag. ch. justice, Leeward Islands, Dec., 1900; ch. just., June, 1904.

URICH, Frederick William, C.M.Z.S., F.E.S.—Ed. in Trinidad, Real Gymnasium, Coblenz, and Geneva Univ.; ledger keeper, govt. printing dept., Trinidad, Jan., 1895; acctnt., rly. extensions, Aug., 1895; 2nd clk., educ. dept., Jan., 1899; store-keeper, P.W.D., Mar., 1901; acctnt., educ. dept., Sept., 1905; also clk. to coll. coun., Oct., 1906; ch. clk., educ. dept., and asst. inspr. of schls., Dec., 1906; mem. of bd. of management and hon. sec. to Victoria Inst., 1894 to 1895, and 1899 to 1901; ag. sec. to agric. soc'y., May to June, 1894; ag. sec. to bd. of educ'n., Feb. to Apr., 1900; ag. statistical clk. and librarian, col. secretariat, Apr. to Oct., 1907; ag. forest offr., Apr. to Oct., 1908. holds a comnr. as lieut. in local forces, Trinidad, since 1897; capt. and adjt., T.L.I.V., 1908; seconded to dept. of agric. as entomologist, 1909.

USHER, Henry Chas., I.S.O. (1903).—B. 1838; Clk., col. sec.'s office, Honduras, June, 1859; in public treasy., July, 1865; provost-marshal, July, 1869; pol. mag. now called dist. mag., Belize dist., Nov., 1873; in charge of the public treasy., June, 1866, to July, 1867, and Apr. to June, 1869; and of Belize gaol, May to Aug., 1872; has acted as registr. of shipping, survr. of shipping, inquisitor of wreck and casualty, and inspir. of pol.; was marshal of the V.-A. ct., is ex-officio judge of the summary ct., and also coroner of the col.; comnr. of currency under Ord. No. 32 of 1894; ag. col. treasr., collr. of cust., and postmr., harbrmr., and suptdt. of mercantile marine on many occasions from 1883 to 1900; er-
officio regar. of births and deaths, 1885 to 1892; suptd. fire brigade, 1886 to 1895; comsnr. on special duty to the Cays, Aug. to Sept., 1889; ag. col. sec., Aug., 1890; ret., June, 1903.

VALANTIN, W. ADOLPH.—Asst. clk. and messenger, Queen's advoc.'s chambers, S. Leone, Jan., 1878; acted as asst. sec. to Br. consmr. on the N.W. Liberian Budry. Coman. in 1879; clk. to crown solr., June, 1880; acted as clk. to ch. just., 1882; clk. to Queen's advoc., 1883; dep. sheriff, Mar., 1890; clk. to ch. just., Aug., 1891; dep. coroner, July, 1895; ch. clk. atty.-gen.'s chambers, Dec., 1897; curator, intestate estates, Jan., 1902.

VALLÉE, LÉONCE JOSEPH.—Asst. accont., Couva extension, Trinidad, 1879; storekr., San Fernando extension, 1880; paymr. Guaracara exten., 1882; asst. clk. locomotive dept., 1884; ch. clk., 1887; ch. cashier, rly., 1894; ch. storekr., 1894.

VANDERBEEK, J. N., I.S.O. (1903).—Extra clk., col. secy.'s office, Singapore, Sept., 1871; 8th clk., Jan., 1873, and attached to govt. house; 6th clk., Dec., 1875; guardian of govt. house, May, 1877; 5th clk., col. secy.'s office, Apr., 1879; 4th clk., June, 1879; 3rd clk., June, 1880; clk., govt. house, Dec., 1883; financial asst., pol., 1906.

VAN DER MERWE, JOHANNES LODEWIUS.—Served under govt. of late S.A.R. as mining comsnr. from 1885 till British occupation, 1st Sept., 1900; mining comsnr., Barberton, 1885; ag. spec. land-drost, Barberton; chrmn., 'diggers' comtee, Barberton; chrmn., Barberton hosp. bd.; mining comsnr., Johannesburg, 1893; chrmn., Johannesburg hosp. bd.; chrmn., Jameson Raid comsnr., 1895-6; mem. of coman. to inquire into causes of dynamite explosion at Johannesburg, 1896; mem. of dynamite relief comtee.; mem. of Johannesburg liquor comsnr.; pres., Witwatersrand agric. socy.; hon. mem. Witwatersrand chamber of mines; served during Anglo-Boer war, 1899-1902; prin. clk., townships (mines dept.), Transvaal, 1903; ag. deputy asst. regar. of mining rights, 1903; district regar. of mining rights, Johannesburg, 1906; mem. of trading bd., Witwatersrand, 1907.

VAN DE VELDE, MARCEL ARTHUR MAURICE.—Ed. at Mt. St. Mary's Coll., Derbyshire; col. audit branch of E. and A. dept., 29th May, 1900; asst. audr., E. Africa Prot., 9th Mar., 1903; asst. audr., Uganda Prot., June, 1903; E. Africa Prot., June, 1904.

VANE, HENRY G. B.—B. 1861; asst. audr., Perak, Dec., 1884; ag. asst. audr.-gen. S.S., Apr., 1887; audr., Sungei Ujong and Negri Sembilan, May, 1888; treas., pol. mag., etc., Sungei Ujong, Oct., 1890; audr., Selangor, Dec., 1892; state audr., Perak, Apr., 1895; rev. audr., Perak, Jan., 1903; ag. fin. comsnr., Oct., 1903, to Oct., 1904; ch. audr., cent. audit off., Jan., 1904; ag. finance comsnr., Oct., 1906, to 31st Jan., 1907; treas., F.M.S., 26th Nov., 1906.

VAN EEDEN, WALTER CLARENCE.—Entd. cust. dept., B. Guiana, 1891; lieut., B.G. militia, 1897-1900; Hythe schl. of musk. certif. for musketry and maxim guns, 1899; attached to 2nd batt. Dorsetshire regt., and gained certif. of proficiency, 1899; asst. inspr. of constab., G. Coast, 30th June, 1900; Ashanti war, medal and gratuity, 1900; offr. commdg. dist. of Bole, 1901; lieut., 3rd batt. Dorsetshire regt., Aug., 1901; lieut., G. Coast regt., W.A.F.F., 1901; certif. E. 511, schl. of instr., Chelsea barracks, Dec., 1901; on expedn. against the Fra Fras, 1902; offr. commdg., Black Volta dist., 1902; transfd. to cust. dept., G. Coast, 3rd Aug., 1903; supervisor in charge, Accra cust. dist., 1904; supervisor in charge, S. dist. Frontier preventive service, 1905-7; superv. in charge, Axim cust. dist., 1907, 1908 and 1909; and harmbr., Axim, 1909; attached to lnd. customs, London, during May, 1909; in ch. supervisor, 24th Feb., 1909.

VAN SOMEREN, ROBERT ABRAHAM LOGAN.—Ed. at Edin. Univ. and Royal Coll. of Sur. Edin.; M.B., Ch.B.; spec. univ. certif., Exot. trop. diseases, and certif. of London Sch. Trop. Med.; med. off., E. Africa and Uga Prot., 10th Oct., 1905.

VAN ZIJL, JAMES STRATEN.—Contrv. P.O. savings bank, late O.F.S., Sept., 1897; d.: O.R.C., Mar., 1900.

VARDON, JOSEPH.—M.L.C., S. Aust., 1st comsnr. of pub. wks. and min. of industry, 19th ch. sec. and min. of industry, 1st Mar. to 2nd July, 1905; res. seat in coun., 11th Oct. 1905; and returned in Dec., 1906, to Commw. senate; fresh election ordered in Feb., 1908; he was duly returned.

VAUDIN, WILLIAM MARSHALL.—B. 1866; Royal Coll., Maur.; writer, P. W. D., Maur., 1888; sworn ld. surv., May, 1890; ag. asst. surv., May to Oct., 1890; 2nd learner, P. W. D., Apr., 1891; ag. asst. surv., May, 1891, to 19th 1892; first learner, P. W. D., June, 1893; ag. asst. govt. surv., Dec., 1897, to Sept. 19th asst. surv., Seychelles, Dec., 1900; superint. wks. and surveys, Aug., 1901; chrmn., loc. of health, central dist., Apr., 1902; ag. audr. and mem. of exec. and legis. coun., Seychelles, 9th May to 10th Nov., 1907, and 8th Feb. to 2nd Sept., 1908.

VAUGHAN, CHARLES STEWART.—B. 1866; ed. Harrow and Trin. Coll., Cambridge (M.I. cadet, Ceylon cir. ser., Oct., 1889; off. asst. govt. agt., Ratnapura, Aug., 1891; fiscal, Prov., and off. asst. to govt. agt., Kandy, Jan., 1896; asst. collr. of cust., Trincomalie, Feb., 1898; asst. govt. agt., Vavuniya and Mullaitivu, Sept., 1898; dist. judge, Batticaloa, June 19th; asst. govt. agt., Trincomalie, Feb., 1902; agt., agt., N.C. Prov., June, 1906; Oct., 1907; dist. judge, Kurunegala, Mar., 1909; govt. agt., N.C. Prov., Sept., 1909.

VAUGHAN, CRAWFORD.—M.H.A., Ser. Australia, 1905; treas., and comsnr. of crown lands and immigration, 3rd June, 1910.

VAUTIER, JOHN FRANCIS.—B. 1863; repatriation dept., O.R.C., Dec., 1902; acctnt., govt. relief dept., 1st Nov., 1902; examr. of accs., treas., 1st July, 1904; book-keeper, treas., 4th Apr., 1906.

VECCHIO, THOMAS JOSEPH.—Marshal sup. & bkrpcty. et al., and V.-A. ct., Gibraltar 1866; interp., 1866-76.

VELLA, TOMMASO.—Entd. Malta service, Dec., 1865; clk., May, 1866; dep. collr. of cust., Ins. dep. postmtr., 1896; collr. of cust. and sup. reports, Sept., 1902; postmtr.-gen., May, 1903; mem. of ex. coun. and coun. of govt., 1903.

VELLACOTT, PHILIP NORTHCOTT, M.F. Lond. (hons. in for. and obst. med.) 1895; B.S., 1896; M.R.C.S., L.R.C.P. (Lond.), 1896; F.R.C. (Eng.), 1901; house surg., res. obstetric and gyn. ast., Guy's hosp.; ast. curator of museum, St. George's hosp.; civ. surg., S. African field force, 1901 to 1902; capt., S.A. Constaby., 6th June, 1902; transfd. to O.R.C. govt. serv. as res. med. offr., National hosp., Bloemfontein, 1st Dec., 1902; fellow of R. Inst. of pub. health; deleg. from O.R.C. to 2nd Internat. Congress on School Hygiene.
VENNING, G.—B. 1879; apptd., after compet. exam., ast. clk., and assigned to local govt. bd., May, 1899; after further compet. exam., apptd. clk. of the 2nd div. of the civ. ser., and assigned to W.O., 8th Jan., 1900; transf'd. to C.O., 16th Apr., 1903.

VERNON, J.—Employed in rly. dept., N.S. Wales; chief acctnt. in treas.; auditor gen., N.S.W., and deputy auditor gen. in N.S.W. for Australian Commonwealth, since Nov., 1902.

VERNON, ROLAND VENABLES.—B. 1877; ed. at Clifton and Oxford; scholar of Balliol, 1895-9; 1st cls. mods., 1897; prox. acc. Hertford schr.; Craven schr., 1897; Jenkyns exhib., 1899; 1st cls. lit. hum., 1899; apptd., after compet. exam., clk. in sec.'s dept. inland revenue, Nov., 1899; 2nd cls. clk., C.O., Aug. 13th, 1900; sec. to Trinidad riot comsn., 1903; mem. of managing comtee. of E.P.O.; assist. priv. sec. to Lord Elgin, Jan., 1908; priv. sec. to Col. Seely, 16th Apr., 1908; ag. 1st cls. clk., 20th Dec., 1910.

VERRAN, HON. JOHN.—M.H.A., S. Australia, 1901; premier and commr. of pub. wks., 3rd June, 1910; also min. of mines, 13th Oct., 1910.

VERTUE, GEORGE ELFORD BANNERMAN.—Apptd. 3rd ast., Nyassaland Prot., Jan., 1901; 2nd grade res., Oct., 1906.

VICKERS, EDWARD.—B. 1842; Emmanuel Coll., Camb.; B.A., 1864; called to the bar, In. Tem., Jan., 1868; advoc. in the high ct., Bombay, Dec., 1868; res. mag., Jamaica, Mar., 1888; acted on several occasions as puisne judge, 1894 to 1904; jun. puisne judge, 1st Apr., 1904.

VICTORIA, RIGHT REV. GERARD HEATH LANDER, Lord Bishop of Victoria, Hong Kong.—B. 1861; ed. at Trin. Coll. and Ridley Hall, Camb., B.A., 1884; M.A., 1888; D.D., 1907; consec. at Lambeth Parish Church, 29th June, 1907; curate of St. Bride's, Liverpool, 1884 to 1888; vicar of St. Benedict's, Liverpool, 1888 to 1896; of Litherland, 1896 to 1905; of St. Cyprian's, Liverpool, 1905 to 1907; chrmn., Litherland schl. pd., 1898 to 1903; chaplain to Liverpool dist. lay readers, 1892 to 1905.

VIGORS, CHARLES THOMAS DOYNE.—Ceylon writer, 1878; pol. mag., 1883; ast. collr. of customs, Trincomalee, 1884; ditto, Galle, 1886; ag. off. ast. to govt. agt., S. prov., from Sept., 1886, to Mar., 1888; ag. dist. judge, Kegalla, Apr., 1888; Tangalla, Dec., 1889; landing surrv. cust., Colombo, Nov., 1888, resumed duties, Feb., 1890; ag. pol. mag., Kandy, May, 1894; ast. govt. agt., Matare, May, 1894, resumed same, Jan., 1896; Kalutara, May, 1898; govt. agt., Uva, Aug., 1900; ast. govt. agt., Kalutara, 13th May, 1902; ag. chmn., mun. coun. and mayor of Colombo, May, 1903; ast. govt. agt., Kalutara, Nov., 1903; govt. agt., N. Cent. Prov., May, 1904; ag. govt. agt., W. Prov., June, 1906; govt. agt., N. Cent. Prov., Aug., 1906; ag. govt. agt., W. Prov., Dec., 1906; list. judge, Kurunegala, June, 1908; prin. collr. of cust., Jan., 1909; ag. postmr.-gen., Sept., 1909; ag. govt. agt. and fiscal, W. Prov., Aug., 1909, and Dec., 1909.

VILLIERS, FRANCIS JOHN, C.M.G. (1880).—B. 1851; entered the C.O., Sept., 1869; priv. sec. o. the admstr. of Grigualand W., Oct., 1875, and clk. of the coun.; ag. col. sec., May, 1877, to July, 1880; mem. of legis. coun., 1879; engaged on special service in connection with the annexation of the prov. to the Cape Col. from Nov., 1880, to May, 1881; audr.-gen., Br. Guiana, 1882; ag. govt. sec., at various times between 1883 and 1896; ret., 1898.

VIRET, ALFRED PERCIVAL.—B. 1865; rev. offr., Dominica, May, 1882; sec. bds. of health and quarantine, Aug., 1884; sec. to local comtee., Ind. and Col. Exhib., 1886; confill. clk. to pres., and clk. exec. coun., May, 1886; govt. offr., treas. and quarantine offr., June, 1891; 1st cl. supervisor of cust., G. Coast, Oct., 1897; ast. col. treas., S. Leone, July, 1899; acted as col. treas., S. Leone, from July to Oct., 1899, and from Jan. to Sept., 1901; acted as col. P.M.G., from June to July, 1900, and from Oct. to Mar., 1902; apptd. collector of customs, 3rd Nov., 1902; ag. col. treas., Nov., 1902, to Apr., 1903, and from May to Aug., 1904; selected in May, 1905, to carry out transfer of the Isles-de-Loe to France, under Anglo-French convention of 1904.

VITALIS, NICHOLAS.—Ch. interp. and clk. to consnr., Larnaka, Cyprus, July, 1878; ditto, Nicosia, Mar., 1879; clk. and interp. to Queen's advoc., Feb., 1882; regist., supreme ct., Cyprus, 1905.

WADDELL, HON. THOMAS.—B. 1854; M.L.A. for various districts in N.S.W. since 1887 (with only short interval); col. treas., 1901-4; premier, 1904; col. treas. since 1907.

WADE, HON. CHAS. GREGORY, K.C.—Called to the bar, Inner Tem., 1886; Crown proscr., New S. Wales, 1891; proscr. for West. circuit and cent. crim. ct., 1894, and resigned, 1902; ag. dist. ct. judge and chmn. of sess. on various occasions; M.L.A. for Willoughby, New S. Wales, 1903; M.L.A. for Gordon, 1904; atty.-gen. and min. for just., Aug., 1904; premier of N.S.W., Oct., 1907.

WAGNER, WILLIAM QUINN.—B. 1849; ed. at S. African Coll., Cape Town; sec. to the Krijgsraad under pres. Burgess, in the first Secoeceni war, 1876; filled various ag. appts. in Landdrost's off., Rustenburg, subsequently becoming postmaster and town clk. of that place; served in various capacities under O.F.S. govt., 1881 to 1900; mine inspr., Jagersfontein, 1891 to 1900; supt., refugee camp, Heilbron, O.R.C., May, 1901, to Mar., 1902; joined mines dept., Transvaal, May, 1902.

WAIT, WALTER ERNEST.—B. 1878; ed. Fettes and Edinburgh Univ. (M.A.); cadet, Ceylon civ. ser., Oct., 1902; addl. ast. to govt. agt., N. Prov., and addl. comsnr. of requests and pol. mag., Mannar and Puttalam during pearl fishery, Feb., 1903; ast. land stltnt. offr., May, 1905; lieut., Ceylon Planters' Rifle Corps.

WAKEMAN, GEORGE HERBERT.—Ed. Bradfield Coll., Berks, and Camb.; admitted solr., sup. ct., England, July, 1891; ast. land offr., Hong Kong, June, 1900; J.P., Dec., 1900; ag. dep. land offr. and offl. recvr. in bankruptcy, Apr. to Dec., 1901; ag. land offr. and offl. recvr. in bankruptcy, Jan. to Nov., 1902, and Jan. to Aug., 1905; comsnr. for oaths, sup. ct., Hong Kong, and comsnr. for taking ackmnts. of married women, Aug., 1905; land offr. and offl. recvr. in bankruptcy, Aug., 1905; ag. regiar. of trade marks and patents, Aug., 1910; ag. regiar. of sup. ct., offl. admstr., offl. trustee and regiar. of companies, Sept., 1910.

WALCOTT, HENRY BARCLAY.—B. 1866; excise and customs offr., St. Lucia, 1884; treas. acctnt., 1890; ag. ch. clk., treasy., 1891; ag. ch. clk. and acctnt., St. Vincent, 1892; ag. treasy. acctnt., Grenada, 1892; ch. clk., audit office, Dec., 1893; ag. postmr., 1895-6; ag. ch. of pol. and excise, 1897; 2nd audit clk., col. sec's off., Br. Honduras, 1897; auditor, Feb., 1898; ch. ast. treas., Gold Coast, Jan., 1900; ag. treas., and mem. ex. and legis. couns., dir., pub. offr.'s guarantee fund, mem. bd. of educn., July, 1900, to Jan., 1901, and May to Oct., 1902; ag. comsnr. of police and supt. of prisons, 1901-1902; pres.
Accra town coun., 1901-1902; treas. and collr. of cust., registr. of shipping, pres., quarantine bd., chmn. poor relief comttee, mem. of bd. of educn., mem. ex. and leg. couns., Br. Hond., Mar., 1903; J.P., Apr., 1903; ag. col. sec., 22nd July to 6th Aug., 1905; 10th Nov., 1905, to 12th Aug., 1906, and from 8th May, 1908; collr. of cust. and detaining offr., M.S. Act, Trinidad, 1909.

WALKER, HENRY.—2nd asst., land dept., Br. N. Borneo, Jan., 1883; asst. supt., lands and pub. wks., Kudat, July, 1883; comsnr., land, and recorder of lands, May, 1884; mem. coun., Oct., 1883; ag. supt., P.W. dept., Jan., 1887.

WALKER, HOPSON PUCKNEY, B.A.—Jesus Coll., Camb., 1853; LL.B. (Lond.), M.A. (Melb.); barrister-at-law (Mid. Tem.), 1888; ch. clk., sup. etc., Melbourne, Dec., 1883.

WALKER, JAMES HUTCHINSON.—Ed. Abdn. Univ., M.A. (nat. sci. hon.), 1876; M.B., C.M. (highest hon., Murray scholar, and gold medal), 1878; M.D. 1884; asst. prof., botany, Abdn., 1876; prin. med. offr., N. Borneo, Aug., 1881.

WALKER, JOHN C.—4th batt. Yorkshire regt.; Coorg Nagpore rifles; served with Yorks. I.Y. in S. Africa (two medals with 5 clasps); asst. polit. offr., Somaliland, Sept., 1905; mentioned in despatches, 1906; asst. rea., N. Nigeria, 1910.

WALKER, LT.-COL. R.S. FROWN, C.M.G. (1891).—B. 1850; entered Sandhurst, 1869; ensign 28th foot, 1871; capt., June, 1881; hon. lieut.-col., 1889; A.D.C. to gov., S.S., 1878-9; attached to Perak armed pol., Mar., 1879; dep. comsnr. of the force, Feb., 1880, and in command from Nov., 1882; acted on various occasions as pol. mag., asst. rea., and as sec. to gov.; has received the thanks of govt. several times for his action in dealing with Chinese and coolie disturbances; in command of Pahang expdny. force, 1892 and 1894; ag. sec. to govt., Perak, Oct., 1894, to Aug., 1895; organised Malay States Guides, 1896; and since commands the regt.; ag. Br. rea., Selangor, Sept., 1899, to Jan., 1900; ditto, Perak, Apr., 1900, to July, 1901; ret. 1910.

WALKER, WILLIAM HENRY, B.A.—B. 1864, apptd. 3rd class clk., gov't. genl.'s office, Canada; 1887; promoted to 2nd cla., 1892; 1st cla., 1898; ch. clk., 1908; chf. clk., dept. of external affairs; 1909.

WALL, JAMES HORNE DARRELL.—B. 1871; clk. and storekeeper, Holberton Instit., Antigua, Nov., 1891; shortd. reporter to W. Ind. Roy. Coman., 1897; aud. def. force accts.; ag. ch. clk. to aud.-gen., Leeward and fedrl. acct., June, 1899; also clk. to trade and income tax comsrs., Sept., 1899; ch. clk. to aud.-gen. and fedrl. acct., May, 1900; ag. treas. of Antigua and federal treas., May-Oct., 1909, and Aug., 1910.

WALLACE, LAWRENCE AUBREY, C.M.G. 1910.—Acting admstr., N.E. Rhodesia, 15th May, 1907; ag. admstr., N.W. Rhodesia, Jan., 1909.

WALLACE, SIR WM., K.C.M.G. (1907), C.M.G. (1897).—Senior ex. offr., Roy. Niger Co., 1886; later as agt.-gen., until 1900, when Niger territs. were handed over to H.M. govt.; concld. numerous treaties with native potentates, one with the Sultan of Sokoto, 1894; commanded or served with over 30 expltns.; deputy high comsnr. and senior rea., N. Nigeria, 1900; admtd. govt., May to Dec., 1901, May to Nov., 1903, Apr. to Dec., 1905, and July, 1906, to Apr., 1907 (3 W. African medals, 5 clasps, coronation medal); received Murchison medal from R.G.S. for important services rendered to geography during many years' residence in Nigeria; ret. 1910.

WALLACE, WILLIAM HENRY.—Entd. gr. ser., 1882; sec. of mines, Tasmania, 1883.

WALLACE, WILLIAM THOMAS EWART.—On 4th batt., The King's regt.; S. African Feb., 1900, to Sept., 1902; supt. of telegr. S. Nigeria, 1903-5; asst. supt. of telegr. Africa and Uganda Prots., 21st Dec., 1905.

WALLER, DESMOND DALBYMPLE.—3rd asst., E. Africa Prot., 12th May, 1899; asst., 23rd Sept., 1899; offr.-in-charge of imigtn., Nov., 1902; prot. of imigtn., 1st Apr., 1903.

WALLIS, C. BRAITHWAITE, F.G.S., F.R.S.—Ed. privately from Eton, and at Shrewsbury and Mil. Coll., Oxford; 2nd lieut., 4th Manch. regt., 1894; lieut., 1895; instr. of musk., 1896; capt., 1897; "Special mention" for schl. of instruction, and "extra" certif. of musk., 1896; instr. of musk. to 3rd Border., 1896, and to 3rd Roy. Welsh Fus., 1897; recommded by G.O.C. dist. for performance of duties; nominated for admission to R.I. Corps., 1897; apptd. to S. Leone Prot. Force, 1898; ag. dist. comsnr., 1899; Mendiland bro', and Karene expedn., 1898; Proteus expedn., 1899; twice mentd. in despatches; command of a column; rec. thanks of govt.; Africa medal and clasp; transf'd. to Ist Cameronians, 1899; to India, Oct., 1899; ser. for ser. in Somaliland, 1901; asst. dist. coms., S. Leone, 1901; ag. comsnr., Apr., 1902, to 1903; awarded silver medal and certif. Humane Soc., Dec., 1901, for saving life in Africa; again selected for service in Somal. June, 1903; J.P. for S. Leone; F.R.C.I.; auth. of "The Advance of our West African Empire" and "West African Warfare" (Unwin, 1906).

WALLIS, FREDERICK SAMUEL.—M.L.C., Australia, 1907; ch. sec. and min. of ind., 27th Mar. to 5th June, 1909; ch. sec., 3rd July, 1910.

WALLIS, HENRY RICHARD.—B. 1866; ass't., Chinde, 15th Sept., 1897; Brit. vice-consul, Johnston, 1st Oct., 1897; 1st cls. asst., B. Africa Prot., 1st July, 1898; ag. ch. judicial Jan. to Nov., 1899; rec'd. coms. as H.M. consul, 9th June, 1900; ag. consul, Mozambique, Feb. to Dec., 1901; apptd. vice-consul, Tetu, Apr., 1901; ag. dep. comsnr., B. C. Africa July, 1902, to Feb., 1903; asst. dep. coms., 1st Apr., 1904; ag. comsnr. and comdr-in-ch., B.C. Africa Prot., May to Nov., 1905; ag. coms., Mar., 1907; asst. dep. gov., Oct., 1907; ag. dep. gov., and govt. sec., Nov., 1907; dep. gov. 24th Mar., 1910; ag. gov. and comdr-in-ch., 4th July, 1910; mem. of exec. and couns.

WALPOLE, SIR CHARLES GEORGE, M.A., F.B.A. (1897).—B. 1848; ed. at Eton and at Coll., Camb.; called to the bar, In. Tem., Jan., 1870; went the home (afterwards the S.E.) circuit; dist. ct., Larnaca, Cyprus, 1882; atty-gen. leeward Is., 1889; mem. of exec. and legis. com., acted as ch. just., June to Sept., 1890, and June-Nov., 1890; ag. ch. just., Gibraltar, Nov., 1892; Nov., 1893; ch. just., Bahamas, Jan., 1894; 1897.

WALSH, FRANK.—B. 1854; entered N. Wales civ. ser., legis. assem. dept., 1874; pub. librarian, 1889; mem. internat. exchange 1896.

WALTER, ROBERT, B.A.—B. 1873; ed. Marlborough, and Worc. Coll., Oxford; 1st honours class. mods.; 3rd cls. honours lit. huz. cadet F.M.S., Nov., 1896; passed in Chas. (Cant.), Apr., 1900; ag. asst. coms., of po.
WALTON, HON. SIR EDGAR HARRIS, C.M.G. (1911).—M.L.A., Cape, for Port Elizabeth, since 1898; treas-gen., Feb., 1904, to Feb., 1908; mem. of S. African National Convention in connection with S. Africa Bill, 1909; proprietor and editor of Eastern Province Herald.

WALTON, GEORGE LAIRD, M.I.M.E., I.I.N.A.—B. 1868; ed. Liverpool coll.; B. of T. certif.; engrnr. mag., dept., Lagos, 1899; upt. engrnr., 1902; senr. engrnr., S. Nigeria, 1907; upt. engrnr., 1907.

WALTON, GEORGE O'DONNELL.—Matriculated student of Lond. Univ., June, 1891; called to the bar, Mid. Tem., 17th Nov., 1893; ag. on several occasions as pol. mag., Barbados; judge of the petty debt court of Bridgetown; judge of the ass't. ct. of appeal; ag. pol. mag., Bridgetown and dist. "A" from 21st July, 1902, to 14th Feb., 1903; pol. mag., dist. "F," 9th Dec., 1902; ag. chief just., St. Lucia, 18th May to 29th Oct., 1908.

WALTON, J. E. LAWSON.—Asst. dist. comsnr., E.A.P., 1910.

WARD, C. E.—Asst. dist. comsnr., E.A.P., 19th Aug., 1909.

WARD, DANIEL, K.C.—Sen. mod. and gold medallist in law, hist. and polit. sci., Trin. Coll., Dublin, 1881; M.A., Dublin, 1887; LL.D., Cape of Good Hope, 1891; called to the bar, Mid. Tem., 1881; crown prosecutor, Br. Bechuanaland, 1894; asst. legal adviser, atty-gen.'s off., Cape Colony, 1898; asst. legal adviser, atty-gen.'s off., Transvaal, 1902; legal adviser, 1903; mem. of legis. coun. of the Transvaal, 1903; 2nd puisne judge, O.R.C., 23rd Mar., 1904; author of "Practice at Parliamentary Elections," "The Marriage Laws of the Cape Colony," "Digest of the Criminal Law," etc.

WARD, JOHN CORBETT.—I.Y., S. Africa, 1900-02 (Queen's medal and 4 clasps, King's medal and 2 clasps); Transvaal civ. ser., 1902-04; reg. reg., E. Africa Prot., 1906; reg. of documents, 1906.

WARD, RIGHT HON. SIR JOSEPH GEORGE, K.C. (1907), K.C.M.G. (1901).—Prime min., col. treas., postmr.-gen., comsnr. of electric telegraphs, and min. of defence, New Zealand; rep. New Zealand at Impr. confee., 1907; mem. of Imp. confee. on naval and mil. defence, 1909.

WARD, W. F.—Assoc. Roy. Schl. of Mines, second, (1876).—Analyst, etc., to the govt. of Tanzania, 1872; asst. to Dr. T. Percy and Prof. W. C. Roberts-Austen, etc., in chemical and metallurgical laboratories of Roy. Schl. of Mines, Royal Mint, and Normal Schl. of Science, S. Kensington (1876-80); special apptmt. to Potosi Gold Mining Co., Venezuela (1881); in charge of chemical testing of smoke-consuming appliances at exhibition, S. Kensington (1881).

WARDOCK, ALEXANDER TURNER.—B. 1866; served with S. Stllnta. pol., 1889-1890; joined S.N. Borneo constab. as storekeeper and orderly-room clk., 1st July, 1890; whilst connected with constab. performed the following duties on various occasions; sg. chief gaoler, sub-editor and charge of P.W.D., 16th June, 1894; in charge of govt. printing office, 1st Sept., 1894, and of P.W.D., 5th Dec., 1894; second in command of Dyak Jubilee contingent, 1897 (medal); resigned, 30th April, 1898; second in command of Dyak Coronation contingent, 1902 (medal); rejoined the ser. as capt.-supty. of civ. pol., and inspr. of sanitary bd., Sandakan, 2nd Oct., 1902; served in S. African War, wounded and shot four times (medal with five clasps); bronze medal for saving life; B.N. Borneo Company's medal, Mat Sallah expeditn. (with clasp "Punitive"); apptd. U.S.A. consul. agent, Sandakan, 1st July, 1904; J.P. for B.N. Borneo; gen. pub. prosecutor for N. Borneo, 1907.

WARING, EDWARD LENNON.—Ed. at St. Paul's schl. and Crystal Pal. Engrnr. Compy. Schl.; asst. engrnr., Uganda rly., 1900-03; asst. ch. survr., E. Africa Prot., 27th July, 1903; dep. dir. of surveys, cadastral branch, 1st Apr., 1906.

WARNER, GEORGE BRUNTON.—Extra clerical asst., G.P.O., P.M. Burg., from Sept. 1st, 1881, to Feb. 16th, 1st-82; 3rd class clk. civ. ser., and filled the post of 7th clk., G.P.O., Feb. 16th, 1882; as 6th clk., Jan. 18th, 1883; clk., col. engineer's dept., Jan. 13th, 1886; border customs offr., De Jager's Drift, Jan. 8th, 1887; issuer of native passes, Dundee div., Jan. 16th, 1888; sheep inspr., De Jager's Drift, May 7th, 1888; J.P., Dundee div., Dec. 13th, 1892; chief examining offr., Customs Point, Durban, Nov. 21st, 1896; ag. clk. of the court, Newcastle, June 16th, 1900; clk. of the court, Newcastle, Aug. 9th, 1900; J.P., Newcastle div., Aug. 16th, 1900; deputy registrar special court, Newcastle div., Aug. 23rd, 1900, in terms of sec. 25 of Act No. XIV., 1900; has acted as asst. and ag. mag. of Newcastle on many occasions; also for the following periods:—Ag. asst. mag. from Nov. 19th, 1900, to March 24th, 1901; ag. mag. from June 6th, 1901, to Sept. 8th, 1901; ag. asst. mag., Sept. 9th, 1901.

WARREN, A.—Apptd. asst., treas., O.R.C., 23rd July, 1901; asst. book-keeper, funds dept., 1st July, 1903; acctnt., funds dept., 1st July, 1905.

WARREN, Lieut.-Gen. Sir CHARLES, R.E., K.C.B., G.C.M.G. (1885), K.C.M.G. (1883), C.M.G. (1878).—B. 1840; ed. Chelt. Coll.; was specially employed in various military and administrative capacities in Griqualand W. and the Cape Col. in 1876-8; lieut.-col. for distinguished service; adminstd. govt. of Griqualand W., 1879 to 1880; served in Egyptian campaign, 1882, and brought to justice the murderers of Prof. Palmer and his party; H.M.'s special comsrr. in Bechuanaland, 1884-5, with local rank of maj.-gen., comdg. expdn.; apptd. to command at Suakim, with rank of maj.-gen., and as gov.-gen., 1886; comsrr. of metropol. pol., 1886-8; C.R.E., and in command of troops with rank of maj.-gen., Singapore, 1889 to 1894; commanding a div. in war against Transvaal and Orange F. S., 1899-1900.

WARREN, ERNEST, D.Sc. (Lond.)—Demonstrator of zoology at Univ. Coll., Lond., 1894; life mem. of convocation of the Univ. of Lond., 1898; asst. lecturer and museum curator at Univ. Coll., Lond., 1899; elected fellow of Univ. Coll., 1898; asst. prof. of zoology at Univ. Coll., 1900; mem. of the faculty of science, Univ. of Lond., 1902; dir. of Natal govt. museum, 1st Feb., 1903.
